entities.name: main road (the outer road east of the moat bridge)
entities.what: The road out of the gate continues east off the moat bridge as a broad open market ground: stalls under mat awnings and big parasols on its north side at the bridgehead, the side open ground climbing north at u 10100-10750, the courier post's ditch and small bridge on its north side, the fortune-teller and the official hall at its east end; on its south side the roofs of a row of large tiled buildings. No edge, kerb or paving is drawn; it is bare earth.
entities.vis: part: edges hidden behind stalls, carts, trees and the south-side roofs
entities.note: No road edge or centre line is drawn anywhere; every point is est, read from where the open ground stops. SEAM WITH S5: centre starts at S5's road end (9400,1370) = the S4 datum (station +26.05). edge_s starts at S5's last edge_s point (9400,1575, the near railing line of the moat bridge continued). edge_n starts at the moat bridge's NE corner (9455,1168 est; S5's edge_n ends 35 px west of it on the same far-railing line at (9420,1168)) and then turns NE to the front of the bridgehead stall. EDGE_N, west to east: the bridgehead stall under the mat awning (9355-9600) and the parasol stalls (9600-10100) stand on its north side, their bases hidden behind the big covered cart (S5.veh.covered_ox_cart_9800); the line follows the foot of their goods and baskets (big basket foot ~(9950,1130)). At u 10100-10760 the side open ground (S4.road.side_ground_10400) opens north: the line is drawn straight across its mouth from the SE corner of the mat-awning stall (~10240,900) to the foot of the two set-down sedan chairs (~10650-10900, v 800-820). u 10900-11140: the line of willow trunks (bases per the tile agents' trees). u 11140-12000: the south (near) bank of the courier post's ditch (S4.grd.ditch_11570), measured at 11200-11450 and 11650-11740, and the small bridge's foot (11712,845). u 12000-12550: the foot of the fortune-teller's tables (~880) and the gnarled base of the big tree (~960-990). u 12550-12750: the front edge of the official hall's platform (v 953-970). EDGE_S, west to east: from the seam along the east edge of S5's willow clump (to ~9640) and then along the silk's bottom edge (v ~1785): between the willow clump and the first south building the open ground runs off the bottom of the silk (figures stand there at v 1700-1770), so the road's south edge there is beyond the painting. Then up the west wall of S4.bld.south_hall_10330 to its NW corner (10350,1590 est) and along its north wall; then the north walls of the thatched hut and the tiled halls further east. All these walls are hidden behind their own roofs: each is est as the visible ridge line (v ~1090-1150) plus ~245 px (ridge ~5.5 m high minus half a ~7 m depth), or the north eave plus ~300 px. A figure standing behind the ridge of S4.bld.south_hall_12100 at u 12150 (feet hidden, est ~1210) and the oxen walking at v 1080-1100 just above S4.bld.tiled_hall_11080's ridge bound it. Low confidence for edge_s east of u 10350. CENTRE: drawn through the traffic (S5's cart and its oxen 9700-10000 v 1250-1450; the second covered cart's wheels ~1250 at 10400; the oxen and rider ahead of it, hooves 1060-1100 at 10600-11000; walkers at 1000-1150 further east), about midway between the edges. The road rises up the silk eastward (centre v 1370 at the seam to ~1070-1220 at u 11000-12750).

Centre through the porter's feet (~10410,630) and the pigs (10150-10300, v 340-430). The ground is ~500 px wide at its mouth and ~300 px at its head; it is open ground, not a lane between walls.

entities.name: ditch in front of the courier post
entities.what: A narrow ditch running east-west between the soldiers' ground in front of the courier post's wall and the main road; its far (north) bank is faced with horizontal planks held by small capped stakes at u 11140-11510 and 11895-11995; the small bridge crosses it in front of the gate. No water is drawn in it (blank silk).
entities.vis: part: west end behind figures; middle stretch only a line; roots of the willow cross the planking
entities.note: WEST STRETCH (u 11140-11510, clear): six horizontal plank lines at v 712, 727, 740, 755, 768, 782 form the far bank's face (about 70-78 px tall), a small capped stake stands in it at 11400-11410 (v 745-790), the willow roots at 11270-11330 hang over it; the near bank is a curved line (11200,808)->(11350,822)->(11450,822) that turns up at its east end (11490,800)->(11510,730) to meet the far bank: a rounded east end. MIDDLE (11510-11740, weak): only a long thin line at v 718-733 (the far bank) and a faint line at v 840-850 (11650-11740) are drawn; between them blank silk. Read as the ditch continuing to the bridge, conf low; it may be dry ground with a low step. BRIDGE: S4.str.small_bridge_11800 at 11712-11895. EAST STRETCH (11895-11995): planks at v 760, 775, 790, 805 with a capped post at 11980-11990 (v 755-810), bottom line 810-815, a second line 830-840; east end hidden by the fortune-teller's crowd (est ~12000). ALTERNATIVE READING: the restyle draws the planking as a low rail fence standing on the ground (and the bridge as a fence heaped with brushwood). The plank lines end on the rounded curve at 11500 and sit above a separate lower curve, which reads as a planked ditch bank; with the small bridge (sections.md: a small bridge in front of the gate) the ditch reading is preferred. SCALE CUES (px): far bank face 70-78 tall (≈1 m deep); ditch width 110 px of v (712->822). DEPTH DIRECTION: the west stretch's rounded east end (11460,805)->(11510,725), slope -1.6, ground, low conf (a curve, not a straight edge).

The restyle reads it as a fence with brushwood; scholars call it the small bridge. SCALE CUES (px): deck 183 px across (E-W, 11712-11895, ≈2.4 m at 77 px/m); 117 px of v from the road end to the post end (845->728, ≈2.3 m of depth); hump ~40-60 px above the ditch banks. DEPTH DIRECTION: west side (11712,845)->(11762,728), slope -2.34; it is the bridge's side at ground level but humped, so low conf.
